chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a man who kills a woman deliberately, and the woman’s family wants to kill him, he said: “That is for them, if they pay to his family half of the diyah. And if they accept the diyah, then for them is half of the diyah of a man. And if a woman kills a man, she is killed for him, and they have nothing except her life.”

And he said: “The wounds of men and women are equal: the tooth of a woman for the tooth of a man, the clarifying head-wound of a woman for the clarifying head-wound of a man, and the finger of a woman for the finger of a man, until the wound reaches one-third of the diyah. Then when it reaches one-third of the diyah, the diyah of the man becomes doubled over the diyah of the woman.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial blood-compensation due in cases of killing or injury
key_terms.ثُلُثَ: one-third; the threshold mentioned for diyah calculation
key_terms.جِرَاحَاتُ: wounds or bodily injuries subject to legal compensation
key_terms.مُوضِحَةُ: a wound that exposes the bone
key_terms.نَفْسُهَا: her life alone; meaning no additional compensation beyond retaliation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on qiṣāṣ and diyah between a man and a woman in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings on retaliation and diyah between men and women in cases of intentional killing and bodily injury. It states that qiṣāṣ for a man who intentionally kills a woman is available upon payment of half the diyah to his heirs, while injury compensation remains equal up to one-third of the diyah before the legal distinction applies.
